_doc: The Cordon wall (DESIGN §1): the precast line round the valley, its Route 9 gate and the culvert that carries it over the Tamsin where the river leaves the valley (main-map region D7, placed by the region), and the Program notice board of Waystation 9 (POI waystation_9_post). Models: tools/assetgen/blender/generators/props_cordon_wall.py -> models/props/<id>[_worn].glb. Axes (Godot): +X along the wall, +Y up, +Z = the VALLEY side (inside the Cordon; the stencilled QUARANTINE BOUNDARY face), -Z = outside. The wall pieces' origin is ON THE WALL LINE at the foot (the river pieces': on the river bed), not the centre of their footprint, so they tile along a polyline: put each piece's origin on the line, rot = the line's direction (rot 0 runs along +X with the valley to +Z). size = [x, y, z] in metres measured from the clean model; boxes are the collision (they mirror the generator's colliders) and their `at` is each box's base centre. standin 'boxes': before `make assets` the model is drawn as its boxes (ModelLibrary), so the wall still reads and blocks.

defs.name: Cordon Wall
defs.description: Six metres of the Cordon: four grey precast T-wall segments six metres tall on one line, a concertina coil and barbed strands on outrigger posts along the top, QUARANTINE BOUNDARY - DO NOT APPROACH THE WALL sprayed on the valley side, CORDON AUTHORITY - RESTRICTED LINE on the other.
defs._tiling: PITCH 6.0 m: the panel runs x -3.0..+3.0 with flush ends (the concrete stops at +-2.985, a 3 cm joint like the joints between its own segments; the wire runs to +-3.0 so neighbours' coils meet). Panel i of a straight run stands at start + (i + 0.5) * 6.0 along the line. The inverted-T base is 1.5 m deep (z -0.75..+0.75), 0.36 m high; the stem 0.36 m thick at its foot, 0.22 m at the top (6.0 m); wire to 6.9 m. At a bend, turn the next panel about the shared end point; the bases overlap on the inside of the bend.

defs.name: Cordon Gate, Route 9
defs.description: Where Route 9 met the Cordon: a T-wall pier at each side, a steel gantry between them with the red CORDON GATE - ROUTE 9 / CLOSED BY ORDER 14 plate and two floodlights, two barred swing leaves chained and padlocked in the middle under a coil of razor wire, and the checkpoint booth on the valley side.
defs._tiling: Two panels' pitch: 12.0 m, x -6.0..+6.0 flush, so it replaces two cordon_wall_panel in a run (its origin where the shared end of those two would be). Piers x +-4.5..+-6.0 (as the panel's segments); the leaves fill the 9.0 m between them (closed: nothing passes); the road's centreline is x 0. The booth stands on the valley side in front of the right pier (x 3.85..5.85, z +1.05..+3.05; door on its road side, -X, z 1.45..2.35, enterable). The footprint is not centred: z -0.75 (the piers' base) .. +3.56 (the booth's sandbags).

defs.name: Cordon Sluice
defs.description: One bay of the culvert that carries the Cordon over the river: concrete half-piers with cutwaters on the upstream side, a lintel wall over a water opening five metres wide and three and a half high, filled by a steel trash rack the water runs through and nobody does, DANGER - SLUICE 9 - NO ENTRY stencilled over it, a dark waterline.
defs._tiling: PITCH 6.0 m like the panels: x -3.0..+3.0 flush; side by side, two bays' half-piers make one 0.8 m pier and their half cutwaters one full nose. The origin is on the river BED under the wall line (the apron's top); the water opening is x -2.6..+2.6, y 0..3.6 (keep the water surface under ~3 m); the concrete tops out at 8.0 m, wire to 8.9 m. Depth z -1.2..+1.2 (+1.75 at the cutwaters, which point upstream: +Z, the valley side, since the river leaves the valley). A 14-26 m river takes 3-5 bays between two cordon_river_abutment. Set the bays' y so their top meets the bank panels' (bed = bank - 2 m keeps the tops level: 8.0 vs 6.0).

defs.name: Cordon Sluice Abutment
defs.description: The mass concrete end of the Cordon's sluice, standing in the bank, with wingwalls stepping down along the river upstream and down to hold the bank.
defs._tiling: 3.0 m along the wall (x -1.5..+1.5); its river face is x +1.5, where the first cordon_river_gate bay butts on (that bay's origin 4.5 m on from the abutment's). The far bank's abutment is the same prop turned 180 (it is symmetric front to back). Origin on the river bed like the bays; 8.0 m of concrete, wire to 8.9 m; the wingwalls run from the river-face corners outward to z +-3.5, flared 32 degrees toward the land, stepping down from 7.7 to 3.0 m. The bank panels continue from x -1.5 (they stand on the bank: put the abutment's y at bank - 2 m for level tops).

defs.name: Program Notice Board
defs.description: A steel-framed board bolted to the wall under a tin hood: PROGRAM NOTICES between two Remand Program roundels, typed notices to salvagers, a sheet of standing orders and a few scrawled slips.
